## Plan-review gate PASSED and CERTIFIED — plus hard data on the sonnet-4-6 grammar timeout

`rebar review-plan aec1-76e7-bb95-4c86` -> **exit 0, verdict PASS**, and
`--status` -> `{"ok": true, "verdict": "certified", "verified_at_sha":
"4b5a7bcd4adf744d96ba98fcd953afa3c37d780e", "signed_at": 1785956593907797000}`.
Obtained with **`REBAR_LLM_STANDARD_MODEL` UNSET**, on stock `sonnet-4-6`, with **no `--force`**.

### Evidence bearing on rebar ticket 895c (sonnet-4-6 native-structured-output grammar timeout)

This is the first question of its kind answerable **by query instead of by re-running**, which is
the whole point of this ticket. Source: `.rebar/usage.jsonl`, 73 recorded calls across
plan-review runs 3-5.

**The 185s signature is REAL and reproducible — 895c's root cause is corroborated:**

    17:36:11  plan-review-prerequisite-verifier  dur=185.6s  requests=0  sonnet-4-6  FAILED
    18:10:23  plan-review-prerequisite-verifier  dur=185.7s  requests=0  sonnet-4-6  FAILED
    18:37:06  plan-review-prerequisite-verifier  dur=185.6s  requests=0  sonnet-4-6  FAILED
    19:03:10  plan-review-prerequisite-verifier  dur=185.6s  requests=0  sonnet-4-6  FAILED

Four occurrences, all on the same step, all 185.6-185.7s, all `requests=0` — no model request
ever completed, exactly what a pre-response 400 looks like. That is a tight, deterministic
fingerprint and it matches 895c's described ~180s grammar-compilation timeout.

**But it does NOT cause INDETERMINATE, and does NOT block certification.** The attestation was
signed at **19:03:13 UTC** and the failure above is at **19:03:10 — three seconds earlier, inside
the very run that passed and signed.** The step degrades; the review still completes and signs.

**So "retrying is futile without the env var" is falsified here:** a certified PASS was earned
without it. Recommend 895c narrow the claim from "the run cannot be verified" to "this one step
degrades", unless there is a separate case where it is genuinely fatal.

**What the verdict actually tracked was the plan findings, not the timeout.** The 185s failure
was CONSTANT across runs 3, 4 and 5, while the verdict moved:

    run 3: blocking 0, advisory 1, indeterminate 14  -> INDETERMINATE   (185s failure present)
    run 4: blocking 0, advisory 0, indeterminate  3  -> INDETERMINATE   (185s failure present)
    run 5: blocking 0, advisory 0, indeterminate  0  -> PASS + CERTIFIED (185s failure present)

A constant cannot explain a variable. The indeterminate count fell 14 -> 3 -> 0 tracking exactly
the findings addressed each round (declaring `run_shape`/`shape_only` as NEW work rather than
citing them as pre-existing was the single biggest one — plan-review reads the ATTESTED
`gerrit/main` snapshot, where a change's own new symbols legitimately do not exist yet). So the
plan edits were not a red herring on this ticket; they were the operative variable.

**A second, DISTINCT failure mode also shows up**, which is not the grammar timeout and should
not be folded into 895c:

    18:17:37 / 18:23:03 / 18:28:45 / 18:43:09 / 18:48:24  overlap-judge  312-381s  requests=3  FAILED

Real requests completed (`requests=3`) and durations are 312-381s, not ~185s. Different shape,
different cause. Overall across the three runs: 64 ok / 9 failed = 12.3% call failure rate.

**Caveat:** these are 4 samples of the timeout on one step of one ticket, from one host. They
corroborate the fingerprint; they do not establish the mechanism (I did not capture the Bedrock
400 body). 895c's schema-complexity analysis remains the mechanism of record.
